target_truth_scope: ClayCode semantic-state expressibility proxy only; not normative ClayCode compiler, not H1/H2, not live FRANK, not Ubuntu target-host evidence

method_negative_result.description: The first reproducibility run used an over-strong stale-candidate oracle that required candidate state to be None after a rejected stale request. Random streams exposed a valid prior-candidate case, causing the oracle itself to fail. The invariant was narrowed to the intended law: a rejected stale or over-budget candidate request must leave the prior candidate state unchanged.
method_negative_result.impact: Test oracle corrected; no ClayCode semantic claim was promoted from the failed run.

inference.supported: The currently required MVC control-state laws can be represented as ordinary typed/versioned state transitions without demonstrating a need for a new dedicated ClayCode language primitive.

next_discriminating_test: Compile the MVC state corpus through the normative ClayCode parser -> canonical typed IR -> type/effect -> evaluator/lowering pipeline, then execute the same transition and mutation corpus; after BASE release, run H1-vs-H2 differential replay on Ubuntu with real learner state receipts.
